title: Coherent cocartesian incidence sections with a fixed source simplex
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, ordinary nerves, quasicategories, mapping spaces and initial objects of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], joins of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone], inner fibrations and cocartesian edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], trivial Kan fibrations of [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration], and categorical equivalences of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Let $C,J$ be small ordinary categories such that no two nonidentity arrows of $J$ are composable. Let $p:E\to N(C)$ be an inner fibration of quasicategories, $d\geq0$, $\tau:\Delta^d\to E$, and $g:\Delta^d\star N(J)\to N(C)$ restricting to $p\tau$. Put $x=\tau(d)$ and let $g_0=g|_{\{d\}\star N(J)}$. For every object $a\in J$, let $f_a:p(x)\to g(a)$ be the corresponding cross edge of $g_0$, and suppose a $p$-cocartesian lift $s_a:x\to y_a$ of $f_a$ is specified.

For each $k$, let $L_k$ consist of pairs $(\sigma,h)$ with $\sigma:\Delta^k\to N(J)$ and $h:\Delta^d\star\Delta^k\to E$ restricting to $\tau$ and satisfying $ph=g\circ(\operatorname{id}_{\Delta^d}\star\sigma)$; use last-block restriction as the simplicial operators. Define $L^0$ similarly with $\{d\}$, $x$ and $g_0$ in place of $\Delta^d$, $\tau$ and $g$. Write $\rho:L\to N(J)$ and $\rho^0:L^0\to N(J)$ for projection. Then $L,L^0$ are quasicategories and last-vertex restriction $R:L\to L^0$ is a trivial Kan fibration over $N(J)$ and a categorical equivalence. For $a\in J$ put $J_a=L\times_{N(J)}\{a\}$ and $J_a^0=L^0\times_{N(J)}\{a\}$. Both are quasicategories; the induced $R_a:J_a\to J_a^0$ is a trivial Kan fibration and a categorical equivalence. Every vertex $z\in J_a$ with $R_a(z)=s_a$ is initial in $J_a$, and such vertices exist.

There is a section $i:N(J)\to L$ with $\rho i=\operatorname{id}$, for which the last edge of the extension $i(a)$ is exactly $s_a$. Its terminal evaluation $N(J)\to E$ carries every arrow of $J$ to a $p$-cocartesian edge. More precisely, any specified vertices $z_a\in J_a$ with $R_a(z_a)=s_a$ can be retained as the vertices of such a section. All of $\tau$, including its earlier vertices and higher faces, stays fixed. These assertions include $d=0$ and $J=\varnothing$.

source.place: Theorem 3.1.2.3 proof, printed p. 336 (last-vertex slice restriction, opposite of its first-vertex form) and pp. 340-341 (initial objects of fixed-base extension categories); Gepner-Haugseng Appendix A.3, Theorem A.3.4, incidence refinement. Generic coherent-section and whole-simplex initiality lemma extracted from returned Step 8; read retained sandbox source/HA.pdf and source/GH.txt. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical assertion.

proof.text: First consider the last-vertex version. Set $B=N(C)$, $b=p(x)$, and $U=E\times_B N(J)$, using the terminal-block restriction of $g$. Nerves of ordinary categories are quasicategories: an inner horn specifies its chain of arrows, and composition gives the missing faces. The pullback $U\to N(J)$ is inner: project a horn to $E$, fill over the given simplex of $N(J)$ using $p$, and pair the filler with that simplex. Hence $U$ and its vertex fibers $E_{g(a)}$ are quasicategories. Apply [lem-cbc-relative-coslice-left-fibration] to $q=p$, $K=\Delta^0$, $K_0=\varnothing$ and $f=x$. Its map $E_{x/}\to E\times_B B_{b/}$ is a left fibration. The map $U\to E\times_B B_{b/}$ sends $(y,\sigma)$ to $(y,g_0|_{\{d\}\star\sigma})$. Its pullback is precisely $L^0\to U$, degree by degree. Pullbacks of left fibrations are left fibrations by the same coordinatewise horn-lifting argument. Thus $L^0$ is a quasicategory. Restricting this pullback to $E_{g(a)}$ gives a left fibration $J_a^0\to E_{g(a)}$, so $J_a^0$ is also a quasicategory. The identification uses only the join-coslice definitions, including the last-block operators.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.6.8, coslice dual, with empty K_0; definition-level pullback application.

proof.text: The inclusion $j:\{d\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^d$ is right anodyne. For $d>0$, identify $\Delta^d=(\Delta^{d-1})^{\triangleright}$ and $\{d\}=\varnothing^{\triangleright}$; apply [lem-coef-infinity-cone-mono-right-anodyne] to the monomorphism $\varnothing\hookrightarrow\Delta^{d-1}$. For $d=0$ the inclusion is the identity, included in the right anodyne class by its definition.

source.place: Right-cone special case of the right-anodyne join calculus; the cone-monomorphism node supplies the class membership.

proof.text:
For $k\geq0$, a boundary lifting problem for $R$ specifies a map into $E$ on
$$P_k=(\Delta^d\star\partial\Delta^k)\cup_{\{d\}\star\partial\Delta^k}(\{d\}\star\Delta^k)\subseteq\Delta^d\star\Delta^k,$$
with the fixed restriction $\tau$, over the simplex $g(\operatorname{id}\star\sigma)$ in $B$. By [lem-coef-infinity-anodyne-cocones], applied to $j$ of step 2 and $\partial\Delta^k\hookrightarrow\Delta^k$, this inclusion is inner anodyne. The inner-fibration lifting condition for $p$ extends from inner horns to their weakly saturated closure: extend on each attached horn, glue at limit stages, and restrict a lift along the section for a retract. It therefore supplies a filler on $\Delta^d\star\Delta^k$. This is exactly a boundary lift for $R$. When $k=0$, the first summand is $\Delta^d\star\varnothing=\Delta^d$, so the same argument proves surjectivity on vertices while retaining $\tau$. By [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration], $R$ is a trivial Kan fibration.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.2.5 and its boundary/pushout-join proof; compare Lemma 2.1.2.3.

proof.text: All these maps retain the $N(J)$ coordinate, so $R$ is over $N(J)$ and $R_a$ is its pullback along $J_a^0\hookrightarrow L^0$. A boundary lifting problem for $R_a$ is a problem for $R$ with base coordinate constantly $a$; its filler still has that coordinate. Thus every $R_a$ is a trivial Kan fibration. By [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-lifts-monomorphisms], $R$ and $R_a$ lift inner horns, since horn inclusions are degreewise injective. Filling the image horn in the quasicategory $L^0$, then lifting that filler, proves $L$ is a quasicategory. The same argument with $J_a^0$ proves $J_a$ is one.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.2.5, base change and inner-horn consequences of boundary lifting.

proof.text: The maps $R$ and $R_a$ have the right lifting property against every degreewise monomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-lifts-monomorphisms]. In the Joyal model structure [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], these are exactly the cofibrations, and the right class of the weak factorization system (cofibrations, trivial fibrations) is exactly the trivial fibrations. Hence $R$ and $R_a$ are Joyal trivial fibrations and therefore categorical equivalences. This proves the categorical-equivalence assertions without assuming any properness of that model structure.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.2.5; categorical-equivalence consequence via the existing Joyal weak-factorization-system statement.

proof.text: At a fixed object $a$, the map $g_0$ over its constant simplices is the constant vertex $f_a$ of $B_{b/}$. Consequently $J_a^0$ is exactly $L(x,f_a)=E_{x/}\times_{B_{b/}}\{f_a\}$ of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality], with all simplicial operators, not merely its set of vertices. That node states that the specified cocartesian lift $s_a$ is initial in this quasicategory. Surjectivity on vertices of $R_a$ supplies at least one vertex $z_a$ with $R_a(z_a)=s_a$.

source.place: Remark 2.4.1.9, opposite-category dual, and surjectivity of the relative slice restriction.

proof.text:
Fix any such $z\in J_a$ and any $w\in J_a$. To show $z$ initial, consider the induced map
$$\operatorname{Map}_{J_a}(z,w)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{J_a^0}(s_a,R_aw).$$
In the right-pinched convention of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], a boundary lifting problem in dimension $k$ for this map is a lifting problem for $R_a$ on the monomorphism
$$((\partial\Delta^k)\star\Delta^0)\cup\Delta^k\cup\Delta^0\ \hookrightarrow\ \Delta^k\star\Delta^0.$$
The initial face $\Delta^k$ is prescribed constantly at $z$, the last vertex constantly at $w$, and the other part by the given boundary. The parts agree on intersections. The monomorphism lifting theorem [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-lifts-monomorphisms] gives the filler, also for $k=0$. Thus the displayed mapping-space map is a trivial Kan fibration. The boundary characterization in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] makes it a weak homotopy equivalence. Its target is weakly contractible by step 6. Composing with the target's map to a point and using two-out-of-three for those weak equivalences shows its source is weakly contractible. Since $w$ was arbitrary, $z$ is initial, as required.

source.place: Remark 2.4.1.9 combined with the right-pinched boundary-lifting specialization; agent-written verification for every prescribed z.

proof.text: For each nonidentity arrow $u:a\to b$ of $J$, restrict $g_0$ to the triangle on $d,a,b$. The two edges $s_a:x\to y_a$ and $s_b:x\to y_b$ define a horn $\Lambda^2_0\to E$ over that triangle; its distinguished edge $0\to1$ is $s_a$. The horn definition of $p$-cocartesianness in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] supplies a filler. Write its third edge as $t_u:y_a\to y_b$. In this triangle the first and long edges are $s_a$ and $s_b$, both $p$-cocartesian. Cancellation in [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] therefore says $t_u$ is $p$-cocartesian. The same node says that degenerate edges are $p$-cocartesian; these will be the images of identity arrows.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.1.8, outer-horn criterion, and Proposition 2.4.1.7, cocartesian dual.

proof.text: There is no nondegenerate simplex of $N(J)$ in dimension at least two: its successive arrows would all be nonidentity, contradicting the hypothesis on $J$. Thus $N(J)$ is obtained by gluing one $\Delta^1$ for each nonidentity arrow to its specified endpoint vertices, with only their degeneracies added. In $L^0$, take vertex $s_a$ at $a$ and the edge corresponding to the triangle of step 8 at $u:a\to b$. The faces of each edge are exactly $s_a,s_b$, so these maps glue to a simplicial map $i^0:N(J)\to L^0$. Its composite with $\rho^0$ is the identity on vertices and generating edges, hence on every simplex. Its terminal evaluation is $y_a$ on vertices, $t_u$ on nonidentity arrows, and the degenerate edge at $y_a$ on an identity. Step 8 therefore proves all these evaluated arrows $p$-cocartesian.

source.place: Agent incidence refinement of the initial-lift construction in Remark 2.4.1.9; the gluing is directly from the ordinary-nerve definition.

proof.text: Now prescribe any family of vertices $z_a\in J_a$ with $R_a(z_a)=s_a$. Let $V=\coprod_{a\in\operatorname{Ob}J}\Delta^0\hookrightarrow N(J)$ be the simplicial subset of vertices and their degeneracies. The family gives a map $z:V\to L$ whose composite with $R$ is $i^0|_V$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-lifts-monomorphisms] to this monomorphism and $R$: obtain $i:N(J)\to L$ with $i|_V=z$ and $Ri=i^0$. Since $R$ is over $N(J)$, $\rho i=\rho^0i^0=\operatorname{id}$. Restriction $R$ leaves the entire terminal block unchanged, so terminal evaluation of $i$ equals that of $i^0$ on every simplex. Its arrows are therefore $p$-cocartesian and its last cross edge at $a$ is exactly $s_a$. By the definition of $L$, each extension still restricts to the entire original $\tau$. For $d=0$, $R$ is the identity and this includes every earlier assertion. For $J=\varnothing$, $L=L^0=\varnothing$ and the unique empty section has all the required properties; assertions indexed by $a$ are vacuous. This completes all clauses.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.2.5 and the monomorphism lifting consequence; prescribed-vertex relative lifting specialized to the incidence nerve.
